## Summary

I located `src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math3/util/MathArrays.java` (2009 lines, already heavily refactored over 16 prior iterations) and made one targeted refactor:

**`checkOrder(double[], OrderDirection, boolean, boolean)`** — hoisted the `isIncreasing(dir)` call out of the per-element loop. Previously `violatesOrder` re-evaluated the `OrderDirection` enum switch on every iteration; now the boolean is computed once and threaded through. This matches the pattern already used by `isMonotonic(T[], ...)`. Behavior is identical (the same condition is evaluated per element); the change just stops redoing the enum switch.

The signature of the private helper `violatesOrder` changed from `(double, double, OrderDirection, boolean)` to `(double, double, boolean, boolean)` — private API only.

**Reverted attempt**: I also tried simplifying `unique(...)` to use `TreeSet.descendingIterator()` (Java 6 API), but the project's animal-sniffer plugin rejects it. Left the original fill-from-end approach intact.

Compiles cleanly; all 64 `MathArraysTest` tests pass.
